Interface AsyncRequestBody

public interface AsyncRequestBody
The body of a request received by the server, read asynchronously, once: a parameter of a controller method or of a request filter method. Nothing is decoded before the method asks for it, and the method chooses how: decoded to a type, as text or bytes, element by element, as a form, part by part, written to a file, or taken as is to pass it on. 
@Post("/people/import")
CompletionStage<HttpResponse<?>> importPeople(AsyncRequestBody body) {
    return body.elements(Person.class)
        .forEach(people::saveAsync)
        .thenApply(done -> HttpResponse.accepted());
}

What a read left open, e.g. the parts of a form that were not read, or a file that is still written, is released when the method completed, normally or exceptionally: when the value or the stage it returned completed, before the response is written or, for a filter method, before the filter chain continues. A read the method did not wait for is aborted then, so the work on the body must be part of the stage the method returns. A controller method that answers with a streamed response, e.g. a Publisher of many items, keeps the body until the stream ends: completes, fails or is cancelled, e.g. the client disconnected, so the stream can be made of the reads of the body. The reads of the copies of the body are released with it.

One read

The body is read once: the first of body(Argument), text(), bytes(int), elements(Argument), transferTo(Path), form(), parts(), takeBody() and discardBody() (and their overloads) owns the body, and a second one fails with an IllegalStateException that names the first. A body that is not read is discarded when the request ends. To read the body more than once, read a copy().

Decoding and failures

body(Argument) decodes the body like a @Body argument of a controller: with the same message body readers, the same media type negotiation, the same limit (micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size) and the same exceptions, so the error routes answer a body that does not decode like they answer it for a controller, e.g. 400 for malformed JSON and 413 for a body that is too large. The returned stages fail with those exceptions; a stage that is returned by the handler reaches the error routes.

Reads that hold the body in memory

body(Argument), text(), text(int), text(int, Charset) and bytes(int) hold the whole body in memory, so they are limited by micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size, however the body arrives. The limit given to text(int), text(int, Charset) and bytes(int) lowers that limit, and never raises it: the body is read up to the smaller of the two, and a larger body fails with a ContentLengthExceededException, answered with 413. A body larger than the buffer limit of the server is read with elements(Argument), which limits each element, written to a file with transferTo(Path), or taken with takeBody().

Streaming

elements(Argument) decodes a JSON array or a JSON stream one element at a time, parts() reads a form part by part, and transferTo(Path) writes the body to a file. Only what the handler asks for is read: the next element or part is received once the previous one was handled. The limits of the server for buffered content apply to what is decoded in memory, a single element or text field; the body as a whole is only limited by micronaut.server.max-request-size. There is no Publisher in this API: a method that needs one can take the body with takeBody().

The body of the request

It is the body of the request the route is invoked with, as the filters left it: the bytes of its byteBody(), which keeps its contract: the request owns the bytes, and a caller that reads them splits them first, like a filter does. takeBody() moves the body to the handler. Reading the body decodes no body for the request: its getBody() does not change.

Copies

copy() returns another AsyncRequestBody over a split of the bytes of the body: reading the copy does not consume the body, which the route, or another reader, can still read in any way. The copy has its own one read, and so does the body it was copied from.

The bytes the copy reads are kept for the body until it is read, so a copy is held to the limit of the server for buffered request content (micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size) as a whole, like a @Body argument of a filter, and a body larger than the limit fails with 413: the streaming reads of a copy, elements(Argument), parts() and transferTo(Path), buffer the body too. A copy is for looking at the body, not for streaming a large upload. form() of a copy is the one form of the request, shared with the form arguments, which do not decode it a second time: the copy reads it from a split of the bytes, unless a form argument read it before, so the route can still read the body in any way, and the form is held to the limit as a whole like the other reads of a copy. parts() of a copy decodes the form a second time, from a split of the bytes.

Filters

A request filter method can read the body with an AsyncRequestBody before the route runs. The arguments of a filter look at the body, the reads of an AsyncRequestBody consume it, and the reads of a copy look at it:

  • A @Body argument reads a buffered copy of the bytes, and the FormData, FileUpload and @Part arguments read the one form of the request, which the filters and the route share: the route can still read the body.
  • Every read of an AsyncRequestBody, body(Argument), text(), bytes(int), elements(Argument), transferTo(Path), form(), parts(), takeBody() and discardBody(), consumes the body: what the filter does not read is discarded, and a route that reads the body after it, with an AsyncRequestBody, a @Body argument or a form argument (FormData, FileUpload, @Part), fails with an IllegalStateException that names the read of the filter, answered with 500. A route that does not read the body answers. These reads are for a filter that consumes the body itself, e.g. to forward it or to reject the request.
  • The reads of a copy() leave the body for the route, which can read it in any way. For a form, a FormData argument or copy().form() is the shared form, which the form arguments of the route do not decode a second time. After a FormData argument the route reads the form, not the bytes; after copy().form() it can read the body in any way, since the copy keeps the bytes, and the body is held to the buffer limit as a whole. copy().parts() decodes the form a second time, for a filter that must stream through the parts and still leave the body for the route.

A filter that reads the body or a copy of it buffers the body before the route can read it.

A filter that continues with a mutable request whose body it set, see MutableHttpRequest.body(Object), replaces the bytes of the request with that body. A body set to null is no body: hasBody() is false, body(Argument) completes like it does for a request without a body, with null for a nullable type and otherwise with the error of a missing @Body argument, text() is empty, bytes(int) is an empty array, and takeBody() is an empty body. A body set to an object is read with body(Argument), which converts it like a @Body argument of a controller: the readers of the bytes, text(), bytes(int), elements(Argument), transferTo(Path), form(), parts() and takeBody(), fail with an IllegalStateException. A filter that continues with another ServerHttpRequest replaces the bytes with its byteBody(). The body is read once either way.

100 Continue

A request that expects 100 Continue is answered with 100 Continue when the body is first read. A handler that answers without reading the body, e.g. with 401, never receives it.

    • body

      <T extends @Nullable Object> CompletionStage<@Nullable T> body(Argument<T> type)
      Decode the whole body to a type, like a @Body argument of a controller: with the message body reader for the type and the Content-Type of the request, and the annotations of the argument. A request without a body completes with null if the type is nullable, and fails like a missing @Body argument otherwise (400).

      The body is buffered: it can be at most micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size bytes. Reactive types, such as Publisher, are not supported: to read a body element by element, use elements(Argument), and to pass it on, takeBody().

      Type Parameters:
      T - The type
      Parameters:
      type - The type
      Returns:
      Completes with the body, null for a nullable type and a request without a body, or exceptionally with the exception a controller's body binding fails with
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the body was already read
      IllegalArgumentException - if the type is a reactive or asynchronous type, or an InputStream

    • elements

      <T> BodyElements<T> elements(Argument<T> type)
      Decode the body element by element: a JSON array (application/json), whose elements are decoded one at a time, or a JSON stream (application/x-json-stream, one JSON value per line). The next element is read when it is asked for. A request without a body has no elements.

      The format is chosen by the Content-Type of the request: a media type with no reader that decodes elements one at a time fails the first BodyElements.next() with an HttpStatusException with the status 415 Unsupported Media Type.

      The readers that decode the elements of JSON one at a time are those of micronaut-http-netty, which the Netty server includes. A server that is not the Netty server, e.g. a servlet server, needs micronaut-http-netty on its runtime classpath to read the elements of JSON: without it, the first BodyElements.next() fails with an UnsupportedOperationException that says so.

      An element is decoded in memory: an element larger than the limit of the server for buffered request content (micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size) fails BodyElements.next() with a ContentLengthExceededException, like a body read whole that is too large. The body as a whole is not limited by it, not even the bytes the server received before the elements are read.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of an element
      Parameters:
      type - The type of an element
      Returns:
      The elements, read as they are asked for. They are closed when the method completed, or when the stream of its streamed response ended
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the body was already read
      IllegalArgumentException - if the type of an element is a reactive or asynchronous type, or an InputStream: an element is decoded whole

    • transferTo

      CompletionStage<Void> transferTo(Path destination)
      Write the body to a new file. The file must not exist, and its directory must exist, like for FileUpload.transferTo(Path): the body is written to a temporary file next to it that is moved to the destination once complete. The body is not held in memory, so the limit of the server for buffered request content (micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size) does not apply.
      Parameters:
      destination - The file to create
      Returns:
      Completes when the file was written
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the body was already read

    • form

      CompletionStage<FormData> form()
      Read the whole submitted form, application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data: text fields in memory, files stored with the micronaut.server.multipart configuration. The files are owned by the request.

      It is the one form of the request, which the FormData, FileUpload and @Part arguments share, but like the other reads it consumes the body: in a filter, the route can no longer read the form, unless the filter reads the form of a copy() or takes a FormData argument instead.

      Returns:
      Completes with the form, or exceptionally with an HttpStatusException with the status 415 Unsupported Media Type when the request has no form body
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the body was already read

    • copy

      AsyncRequestBody copy()
      A copy of the body: another AsyncRequestBody over a split of the bytes, whose reads do not consume this body. The copy has its own one read, and this body keeps its own, e.g. for the route after a filter read the copy. See the Copies section above.

      Nothing is read before the copy is: the bytes are split when it is read. The bytes it reads are kept for this body, so the copy is held to micronaut.server.max-request-buffer-size as a whole, even for transferTo(Path), elements(Argument), form() and parts(), with 413 for a larger body. form() of a copy is the one form of the request, read from a split of the bytes unless a form argument read it before, and parts() of a copy decodes the form again from a split of the bytes. A copy of a body a filter cleared or replaced with an object is that body too: no body, or the object. A copy of a body that was consumed cannot be read either.

      Returns:
      The copy
      Since:
      5.3.0
